title: Northbridge AI x Redwood — Optimize POC check-in (cost model + caching/batching)
topics: Optimize POC status and success criteria
Measured savings from KV-cache + prefix caching
Console cost breakdown enablement and explain endpoint
Telemetry gaps (prefill/decode split, cache hit rate tags, region/SKU)
Next steps for staged rollout and support enablement
questions: Can we see cost broken down by prefill vs decode and cache hits vs misses?
How do you handle missing telemetry—do you show assumptions and confidence?
If we run multi-tenant traffic, how stable is batching efficiency in the model?
Can Console show an ‘estimated’ label and a tooltip with assumptions?
Do you store prompt text for the explain output, or only counters?
next_steps: Redwood to enable Cost Model API + Console breakdown feature flag in Northbridge staging tenant.
Northbridge to share two representative routes (chat + summarization) with target p95 latency SLOs and typical token distributions.
Redwood to provide a one-pager explaining SCM confidence scoring + what triggers ‘low confidence’.
Redwood to confirm which runtime signals are available today (prefill/decode, batch_size_effective, kv_cache_hit_rate) and what is still being backfilled.
Schedule a 45-min follow-up focused on per-route export needs and FinOps reporting (CSV/API).
action_items: Aditya Rao: Send SCM assumptions/confidence explainer (internal draft + customer-safe version) by 2025-02-10.
Dylan Brooks: Coordinate Console cost breakdown flag rollout steps + fallback behavior doc snippet by 2025-02-11.
Hassan Mirza: Run a what-if sweep for Northbridge route ‘/chat/support’ comparing (batching off) vs (batching on target=8) vs (batching on target=16) and share deltas by 2025-02-12.
Erin Walsh: Provide request logs summary (no prompt text) with input/output token histograms and target regions by 2025-02-10.
Kelly Tran: Confirm what internal cost fields are needed for FinOps (per-route, per-model, per-tenant, hourly/daily) by next call.
summary: Northbridge shared early POC results showing meaningful unit-cost reductions when KV/prefix caching is warm and batching is enabled. They’re generally happy with Optimize’s recommendations but want more transparency: how Redwood’s Standard Cost Model (SCM) arrives at an estimate, what assumptions are used when telemetry is missing, and a confidence indicator they can show internally. Redwood aligned that SCM outputs are ‘technical cost attribution/estimates’ (not billing) and that Console can surface breakdown + assumptions via an explain-style payload. Team agreed to enable Console cost breakdown behind a feature flag in Northbridge staging, and Redwood will run additional what-if sweeps to quantify batching targets vs tail latency risk.
transcript:
Fireflies.ai Transcript

Title: Northbridge AI x Redwood — Optimize POC check-in (cost model + caching/batching)
Date: 2025-02-06
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 38 minutes
Recorded by: Fireflies.ai

Attendees (Redwood): Aditya Rao, Hassan Mirza, Yara Haddad, Dylan Brooks
Attendees (Northbridge AI): Erin Walsh, Samir Gupta, Kelly Tran, Jon Park

---
Summary (auto-generated)
- Reviewed week 2 POC results for caching + batching.
- Northbridge requested transparent cost assumptions and confidence.
- Discussed enabling Console cost breakdown and the SCM explain output.

Topics (auto-generated)
1) POC metrics + results
2) KV-cache / prefix caching validation
3) Batching settings and tail latency
4) Cost Model assumptions & confidence
5) Console breakdown enablement + feature flag

Action items (auto-generated)
- Redwood: share SCM assumptions/confidence explainer.
- Northbridge: share token distribution and route list.
- Redwood: enable Console breakdown in staging via flag.

---

[00:00] Aditya Rao: Hey everyone. Can you all hear me okay?

[00:03] Erin Walsh: Yep, good.

[00:04] Kelly Tran: Yep.

[00:06] Hassan Mirza: Loud and clear.

[00:07] Aditya Rao: Cool. So today’s check-in is mainly: quick readout on the caching and batching experiments you ran last week, then a deeper bit on the cost model transparency, because I saw the note about “we need to explain this internally.” And then Dylan’s here because we can talk through enabling the Console cost breakdown for your tenant.

[00:27] Jon Park: Sounds good. We’ve got like thirty minutes.

[00:30] Aditya Rao: Perfect. Erin or Samir, want to start with what you’re seeing?

[00:36] Samir Gupta: Yeah, so… we wired the SDK into two routes. One is a customer support chat flow, the other is like an internal doc summarizer. The big thing is caching. Once we got the cache warm, the costs looked… like, materially better. Like, not a few percent.

[00:55] Aditya Rao: When you say caching, you mean prefix caching plus KV-cache reuse? Just want to be precise.

[01:01] Samir Gupta: Uh yes. The “prefix” one, where the system prompt and the first chunk gets reused. Our prompts have this big policy section that repeats.

[01:12] Hassan Mirza: Got it. That maps to what we call prefix/KV caching. Sometimes the labels are confusing.

[01:18] Erin Walsh: The numbers we saw were something like… on the chat route, once warm, average tokens billed didn’t change obviously, but the runtime… sorry, the compute time dropped. And the SCM estimate in Optimize dropped like ~28% on median.

[01:33] Kelly Tran: The part I care about is: can I show that as “this is why cost dropped” rather than just “trust us.” Like we need a breakdown to justify, because finance is going to ask.

[01:45] Aditya Rao: Yep. That’s exactly what SCM is supposed to support. Right now Optimize is consuming SCM outputs and showing deltas, but Console breakdown is the thing that makes it legible.

[01:58] Dylan Brooks: And also, for your internal teams, you can show it as “estimated technical cost,” not invoice cost. I want to set expectations.

[02:07] Kelly Tran: Totally. Even “estimated” is fine, as long as the assumptions are clear.

[02:12] Aditya Rao: Great. Before we jump to that, on batching: did you enable continuous batching on both routes or only summarization?

[02:21] Erin Walsh: We enabled it on summarization first, because we didn’t want to mess up chat latency.

[02:26] Samir Gupta: And then we tried a small batch target on chat, like “max batch 8.”

[02:33] Hassan Mirza: Okay. And what happened to p95?

[02:36] Samir Gupta: p95 got a bit worse. Not crazy, but noticeable. Like 280ms to 340ms on decode-heavy requests.

[02:45] Jon Park: The product SLO for that endpoint is 400 p95, so it’s okay, but we don’t have infinite headroom.

[02:52] Hassan Mirza: That’s consistent. Batching increases queueing under burst. The important question is if it’s stable at peak.

[03:00] Erin Walsh: Peak is where we were worried. We don’t have huge concurrency yet, but it spikes.

[03:05] Aditya Rao: What about the cost delta on batching?

[03:08] Erin Walsh: For summarization it looked like 15 to 20% reduction on estimated compute. For chat it was smaller because concurrency wasn’t high enough, so it’s like… sometimes it does nothing.

[03:21] Hassan Mirza: Right, batching effectiveness is workload dependent. That’s why in Optimize we try to show “expected savings” and “confidence.”

[03:29] Kelly Tran: Yeah, about that. The confidence thing. How is that calculated? Because I saw “medium” and I need to explain what that means. Like is it statistical or vibes.

[03:39] (crosstalk)

[03:40] Aditya Rao: Yeah, fair. Not vibes. So we have an explicit field in SCM output that lists assumptions used and a confidence score. The score is mostly based on completeness of telemetry signals and how close the scenario is to observed distributions.

[03:56] Dylan Brooks: And for Console, we can surface it as a tooltip. Like “We assumed cache hit rate = X based on last 24h” or “batch efficiency assumed default due to missing signal.”

[04:07] Kelly Tran: That’s exactly what we need.

[04:10] Erin Walsh: Okay but—what signals are you missing today? Because we saw some “assumption: region default” in one run.

[04:18] Hassan Mirza: That’s probably because the request didn’t pass the region tag through. We need region + GPU sku for the normalized compute. Otherwise we use the deployment default.

[04:29] Erin Walsh: For us it’s all us-east-1, but yeah maybe our client didn’t set it.

[04:34] Aditya Rao: Just to clarify: in Hosted, region is known; in Dedicated/Private, we sometimes rely on the runtime tag. But we’re making it more deterministic.

[04:45] Jon Park: We’re on Dedicated right now for the POC.

[04:48] Aditya Rao: Right. That makes sense.

[04:50] Kelly Tran: So SCM is not pricing, it’s cost estimate. But still, what is cost exactly? GPU seconds? Dollars?

[05:00] Aditya Rao: In the output you’ll see both normalized cost units and a currency estimate. The currency estimate is internal conversion using the SKU cost tables—again, not billing. The important piece is breakdown components: compute prefill, compute decode, memory/kv overhead, cache savings, batching efficiency.

[05:20] Samir Gupta: Can you break out prefill vs decode explicitly? Because our long prompts are killing us.

[05:26] Hassan Mirza: Yes. We have prefill_tokens and decode_tokens and corresponding time/cost components, assuming the runtime emits the split. If that split is missing, we infer based on token counts and a model profile.

[05:41] Erin Walsh: That inference part is the thing we need to label clearly.

[05:44] Aditya Rao: Yep. That becomes an “assumption” entry: “prefill/decode split inferred from model profile.” And confidence goes down one notch.

[05:55] Kelly Tran: Okay. And do you store prompts to do that?

[05:59] Dylan Brooks: No, not prompt text. For explain, it’s basically counters and tags: token counts, timings, cache hit rates, quant profile id, model version, region, sku. No raw customer input.

[06:15] Kelly Tran: Good.

[06:16] Jon Park: What about data retention on that telemetry?

[06:19] Dylan Brooks: For the POC, the cost breakdown view is based on short retention. We can discuss longer retention as an enterprise add-on, but the default is limited. Also, access is audited.

[06:31] Erin Walsh: That’s fine.

[06:33] Aditya Rao: Let’s look at your results quickly. Erin, you had a screenshot or numbers?

[06:39] Erin Walsh: I can just read them. For summarization, baseline estimated cost per 1K output tokens was around… sorry, I’m mixing units. It was about $0.18 per request average with our typical lengths. After batching target 16, it dropped to $0.145-ish. With caching warm it’s even lower for the chat route.

[07:02] Hassan Mirza: That lines up.

[07:04] Kelly Tran: That’s bigger than I expected, honestly.

[07:08] Samir Gupta: The big chunk was caching, not batching.

[07:11] Hassan Mirza: Makes sense if prompts repeat.

[07:13] Aditya Rao: And did you see any quality issues? Sometimes quant or batch changes can affect outputs.

[07:20] Samir Gupta: No quality issues. We didn’t change quantization profile, just runtime config.

[07:25] Aditya Rao: Great.

[07:27] Erin Walsh: We did have one weird thing. When cache is cold, the SCM estimate looks like it’s “too optimistic” vs what we measured. Like first requests after deploy.

[07:38] Hassan Mirza: That could be because the cache hit rate assumption is using trailing window, or it assumes steady-state. The model should be explicit: cold vs warm scenario.

[07:50] Aditya Rao: Exactly. For Optimize what-if we run both warm and cold scenarios if we have enough data. If we don’t, we should mark low confidence.

[08:00] Kelly Tran: Can we force it? Like “show me cold start cost.”

[08:05] Hassan Mirza: We can in the what-if inputs. There’s a parameter like “kv_cache_hit_rate = 0” scenario. We’ll do that in the next sweep.

[08:15] Aditya Rao: Hassan can run a scenario sweep for your chat route: batching off vs 8 vs 16, and cache warm vs cold. We’ll send you the deltas.

[08:25] Erin Walsh: Great.

[08:27] Dylan Brooks: On Console: what you’ll see is a per-route breakdown chart with an “estimated” label and then a details drawer with assumptions and confidence.

[08:39] Jon Park: Is that available now or “soon.”

[08:42] Dylan Brooks: It’s behind a feature flag. For your staging tenant we can enable it next week.

[08:49] Kelly Tran: We want staging first.

[08:51] Dylan Brooks: Yep. We can do staging, validate, then roll to prod.

[08:56] Erin Walsh: What’s the fallback behavior if the cost model API is slow?

[09:01] Dylan Brooks: Good question. Console will fall back to cached results and show “delayed” rather than erroring the whole page. Worst case it hides the breakdown module.

[09:11] Kelly Tran: Please don’t block the page. Our execs love dashboards.

[09:15] Dylan Brooks: Understood.

[09:17] Aditya Rao: Also: SCM isn’t on the request path for inference, just for reporting and what-if. So it shouldn’t affect serving.

[09:26] Samir Gupta: Okay.

[09:27] Erin Walsh: For enabling, what do you need from us?

[09:30] Dylan Brooks: Just confirm tenant ID, and the two routes you care about, and what time window. Also, we’ll need the region tags to be correct so attribution doesn’t get weird.

[09:43] Erin Walsh: I’ll send tenant ID and route names.

[09:46] Aditya Rao: While we’re on transparency: Kelly, you mentioned you need to explain “assumptions.” What would be the minimal set of assumptions that are acceptable?

[09:57] Kelly Tran: Like: what hardware cost basis, what cache hit rate was used, what batch size, and whether it was inferred or measured. Also if you normalize across GPUs, like if you’re using A100 vs H100.

[10:11] Hassan Mirza: Yeah. The SCM inputs explicitly include sku, and if we don’t know sku we use a default for the cluster. That gets flagged.

[10:22] Kelly Tran: Great.

[10:23] Jon Park: Also, we’re getting questions internally like “why is decode more expensive than prefill sometimes.”

[10:30] Hassan Mirza: Usually decode is longer wall time per token because it’s sequential. Prefill is more parallel. But depending on attention kernel and batch it can vary.

[10:41] Samir Gupta: Okay.

[10:43] Aditya Rao: We can include that as copy in the Console tooltip. Like “decode is sequential, so cost per token can be higher.”

[10:51] Dylan Brooks: We have a draft of that copy. It’s not perfect.

[10:55] Kelly Tran: Anything is better than nothing.

[10:57] Aditya Rao: Cool. Another question: are you comparing us to anything else right now? Just to understand what you’re showing stakeholders.

[11:05] Jon Park: We’ve used Bedrock for some prototypes, and we tried Together for a week. We also obviously have OpenAI for a couple internal tools.

[11:14] Aditya Rao: Got it. And is the key difference that you want more control over serving economics?

[11:20] Jon Park: Yeah. We can’t just accept opaque costs. We need to predict spend if traffic doubles.

[11:26] Kelly Tran: And I need something I can audit. Doesn’t mean you give me raw GPU invoices, but the model should be consistent.

[11:34] Aditya Rao: That’s literally the goal of SCM—same inputs, same outputs, deterministic.

[11:41] Erin Walsh: Quick tech question: Does the breakdown include “memory” cost? Like KV cache memory footprint.

[11:48] Hassan Mirza: It does as a component. It’s basically an allocation model: kv cache bytes * time * sku memory factor. It’s not perfect, but it captures “bigger context windows cost more.”

[12:04] Samir Gupta: Nice.

[12:06] Erin Walsh: Okay. But we don’t want cardinality explosion. Our metrics pipeline can’t handle like per-user labels.

[12:13] Hassan Mirza: Right. We don’t do per-user. We do per-tenant, per-route, per-model version, region, sku, quant profile id. That’s already plenty.

[12:26] Dylan Brooks: Console also aggregates; you can drill down but not to like request-id by default.

[12:33] Kelly Tran: For finance I mostly need per-route daily totals and trend.

[12:38] Dylan Brooks: That’s on the roadmap. For now, per-route cost over time is in the breakdown page.

[12:46] Aditya Rao: Let’s talk about the “explain” output specifically. The POC question we got was “show me why this got cheaper.” That’s explain: it returns the breakdown plus contributing factors, like cache hit rate, batch_size_effective, prefill/decode ratio.

[13:03] Erin Walsh: Is that an API we can call too?

[13:05] Aditya Rao: It’s internal right now, but we can expose it for your POC if needed. Console will call it.

[13:11] Kelly Tran: Console is enough.

[13:13] Samir Gupta: Same.

[13:14] Hassan Mirza: For the sweeps, we’ll use the estimate endpoint and generate deltas.

[13:20] Aditya Rao: Okay. I want to make sure we’re not missing anything blocking next week. Erin, earlier you said one of the runs had “default region.” Let’s fix that.

[13:30] Erin Walsh: Yeah. I’ll check our integration. Maybe we’re not passing headers.

[13:35] Dylan Brooks: In Dedicated, it’s often in the runtime tag, not the client. But we can confirm.

[13:41] Erin Walsh: Ok.

[13:42] Jon Park: What about access controls? If we enable Console breakdown, can we limit who sees it?

[13:48] Dylan Brooks: Yes, via RBAC. It’s the same role system as the rest of Console. Also, reads are audited.

[13:56] Kelly Tran: Audited how?

[13:58] Dylan Brooks: Basically “actor, tenant, what page/module, timestamp.” It doesn’t log the raw payload. It’s more like an access event.

[14:06] Kelly Tran: Good.

[14:08] Aditya Rao: Zooming out: would you say the POC is on track? Any red flags?

[14:14] Jon Park: No red flags. The main thing is internal buy-in. The savings look real. We just need to communicate it.

[14:23] Kelly Tran: Exactly. If you give me a breakdown with assumptions, I can sell it internally.

[14:29] Aditya Rao: Great.

[14:31] Hassan Mirza: One thing I’d like to request from you: token distributions. Like histograms of input length and output length per route. That makes our what-if recommendations more accurate.

[14:43] Erin Walsh: We can do that. No prompt text.

[14:45] Hassan Mirza: Yeah, no text, just counts.

[14:49] Erin Walsh: Okay.

[14:50] Aditya Rao: And Kelly, you mentioned “auditability.” We have a plan to include a “calculation_version” and “scm_version” in the payload so you can say “this was computed by v1.0 of the model.”

[15:04] Kelly Tran: That’s great. Because we’ve been burned where vendors change something and the numbers move.

[15:10] Aditya Rao: Yep. And when it changes, we’ll keep backward compatibility.

[15:15] Jon Park: Is it like header versioning?

[15:17] Aditya Rao: Exactly. Clients can request a version, and if it’s unsupported we return an explicit error.

[15:24] Samir Gupta: Cool.

[15:26] Dylan Brooks: For Console we’ll pin to v1 until we validate v2.

[15:30] Kelly Tran: Good.

[15:32] Aditya Rao: Let’s spend a minute on the cold start discrepancy. Erin, when you said “too optimistic,” do you mean SCM cost lower than measured?

[15:41] Erin Walsh: Yeah. Like first ~10 minutes after deploy, the runtime is slower, maybe compilation or caching. SCM doesn’t account for that.

[15:52] Hassan Mirza: That’s a real thing. Some of it is kernel warm-up, some is cache not populated. SCM is meant to estimate steady-state cost for inference, not transient warm-up overhead, at least in v1.

[16:05] Kelly Tran: That’s fine, but it should say that.

[16:08] Aditya Rao: Agree. We’ll add an assumption note: “warm-up overhead not included.”

[16:14] Dylan Brooks: We can also show “data window” in Console, like last 1h/24h.

[16:20] Erin Walsh: That would help.

[16:22] Jon Park: So basically we shouldn’t use it to evaluate deploy-time spikes.

[16:26] Aditya Rao: Not initially. Later we can incorporate it as a separate component.

[16:33] Samir Gupta: Makes sense.

[16:35] Aditya Rao: Any other questions on the cost model itself?

[16:39] Kelly Tran: One more. When you say “memory cost,” is it double counting? Like compute and memory are correlated.

[16:47] Hassan Mirza: It’s not double counting in the model, but it is an allocation. Think of it as attributing GPU capacity usage across dimensions. It’s more for explainability than physics.

[16:59] Kelly Tran: Okay, but the breakdown totals still sum to the total?

[17:02] Hassan Mirza: Yes, sums cleanly.

[17:05] Kelly Tran: Great.

[17:06] Aditya Rao: Cool. Then next steps: Dylan will coordinate the feature flag for Console breakdown in staging. Erin, you’ll send tenant ID and route list, plus token histograms. Hassan will run sweeps including cold cache scenario. I’ll send a short doc on assumptions and confidence.

[17:26] Erin Walsh: Works.

[17:27] Kelly Tran: Works.

[17:29] Jon Park: Can we schedule next week same time?

[17:31] Aditya Rao: Yep. Connor from releases will probably want to know the date, but we can do it.

[17:36] Dylan Brooks: Also, if you have internal stakeholders who want to see the breakdown, we can do a quick screen share once it’s enabled.

[17:44] Kelly Tran: Yes please.

[17:46] Aditya Rao: Alright. Anything else before we drop?

[17:50] Samir Gupta: No, we’re good.

[17:52] Erin Walsh: Thanks.

[17:53] Aditya Rao: Thanks all.

---
End of transcript.
